answer: The kernel ties each agent identity to a posted bond of 500 units plus one hardware credential, so a second identity requires a second bond and a distinct device. An attacker registering k fakes locks 500k units, faces 100 percent slashing on proven fraud, and waits three epochs to withdraw. Splitting identities raises marginal cost per fake, since shared bonds carry the full penalty and independent jurors detect duplicate credentials during the lotus reef audit.
